actionable_findings.title: Ready reap loop can exhaust the absolute cleanup deadline before force/census
actionable_findings.evidence: reap_ready loops until waitpid returns pid0 or ChildProcessError. It has no time.monotonic/deadline check; the first deadline check is after this helper and the signal pass. The same unchecked helper is called after force.
actionable_findings.trigger: A live adopted descendant can continually create orphaned children that become immediately waitable by the subreaper. If waitpid keeps returning completed children, the before_force drain never returns even after the shared15s budget; no force, post-reap census or immutable final receipt is reached.
actionable_findings.distinction: The original post-force wait loop also lacked a deadline check. Collector2 adds this unchecked drain before any force, despite the selected design requiring an absolute15-second cleanup bound from entry. This is a narrow acceptance gap in the changed cleanup path, not a request to broaden protocol assertions.
actionable_findings.requested_change: Preserve version2. In a new version, check the shared absolute deadline on each reap pass; explicitly record exhaustion and make it a nonpassing cleanup input. Preserve bounded safe cleanup/census and actual wait statuses. Do not reset/extend deadline, mark incomplete drain naturally clean or weaken main/Actor predicates.
actionable_findings.regression: Add deterministic before-force and after-force mocks for each collector: waitpid remains immediately productive across advancing time; assert return within budget, explicit exhaustion/FAIL and no silently omitted receipt. Existing deadline mock only returns pid0 in reap_ready and checks the later force path.
actionable_findings.production_impact: Collector can fail to terminate/report within required budget. No production protocol defect established.
